analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: MO' RELIEF
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +60bps at 7,722 with a $3.3bn market-on-close imbalance to sell. NDX +129bps at 29,651, R2K +117bps at 2,819, Dow +3bps at 52,377. Volume was 16.136bn shares vs a YTD daily average of 18.503bn.

NDX posted back-to-back 1%+ daily gains for the first time in about 3 months. Investors are debating whether the bounce can become a rally. Breadth was narrow, with about 60% of S&P names lower on the day.

Momentum recovered +2.5% after a ~20% drawdown over the last few weeks. GSPRHIMO high beta momentum is up ~8% over the last 3 sessions. Per GSPB, global fundamental long/short momentum exposure is near YTD lows after the de-grossing episode.
The GS floor rated activity a 4 on a 1-10 scale, with flow skews benign. Asset managers were net buyers of info tech and discretionary and sellers of comm services.

Peter Bartlett's view: supply abatement is driving most of the bounce, as high-velocity supply and length reduction are now largely behind the market. The desk sees emerging but still limited offense across the AI complex, a shift from about zero offense over the last handful of weeks.

Bartlett's base case is that the market stays choppy. Participants likely want more price stability and more risk boxes checked before moving fully to risk-on, given about 3 months of poor performance.
Post-bell, STX fell 7% in a 'sell the news' reaction despite a beat and a guide above, with revenue guided +14% q/q.
Derivatives: SPX fixed strike vols were bid gradually through the session and along the curve. NDX vol outperformed SPX only in the belly of the curve, with gamma and pure vega tenors little changed.
NDX skew steepened in the belly while SPX skew flattened notably, particularly in gamma tenors.
High beta momentum winners (GSCBHMOM) and AI (GSTMTAIP) led the day, which the desk read as offense finally being played.

GS customer flow: bought 66k SPY 20Nov 800 calls and 33k 18Dec 810 calls. In single names and thematics, flows turned bullish with an emphasis on tech and hyperscalers after a painful month for tech-focused funds. The market saw a buyer of 69k AAPL 15Jan 380 calls and a buyer of 50k GOOGL 15Jan 360 calls.

The desk thinks the market has rallied back into a pocket of dealer long gamma and is looking for a catalyst to keep SPX comfortably above 7700. The SPX implied move through tomorrow is 61bps vs 50bps the prior day. Key earnings and the Fed are due tomorrow.
